cells.tense: You are pointed at something and steering by it on purpose right now.
cells.ask: Tell one person the direction you've picked, in a sentence, before the week turns.
cells.core:
You're aimed, and you know you're aimed. The direction isn't inherited and it isn't borrowed — it came from something in you that lit up and stayed lit, and you've been moving toward it without needing the whole route worked out. That's the thing worth noticing: you can pick a way to go and walk by it without arguing the pick.

What makes this steady is that you're not holding it alone. The direction gets carried by what's around you — people, structure, the plain support that shows up when someone actually knows where they're going. Hold it that way. Tell one person where you're pointed, out loud, in a sentence, and let that be the whole of it for now.
cells.sheetLine: You've picked your direction, and you're walking by it.
cells.place: in the part of you that says this, not that

cells.tense: You are already standing in a future the direction was only supposed to point toward.
cells.ask: Wait one day before acting on the next big move, and let the direction stay unchosen until it's chosen.
cells.core:
You've picked a direction and now you're living past it — rehearsing the arrival, defending the route, checking who's on board. The pointing came from vision, and vision doesn't survive being audited this hard. Every question about whether it's really the right way to go pulls you further from the walking.

What you've lost is the comfort of not-knowing. You can hold one certainty without holding all of them. Leave a single thing about the direction undecided on purpose, and don't force it closed. The pull doesn't need proving to keep pulling. Let one move wait, and notice that the direction still points while you do nothing.
cells.sheetLine: You're defending the route instead of walking it.
cells.place: in the part of you that says this, not that

cells.tense: You are still standing at a place you already left, and the door is open behind you.
cells.ask: Pick the smallest next step toward a thing you already love, do it today, and notice it took less than you feared.
cells.core:
There's a direction you can feel, and you're not walking it. The pull is still there — it hasn't gone anywhere — but the picking stopped, and you've been waiting at a place you already left. That's not a lack of vision. Seeing what to move toward is fine. What went quiet was the part that says this, not that and means it.

Don't try to feel your way back. Find one small thing you already tend and let it grow — a scrap of care that doesn't take much from you, something you enjoy having produced. Tending that is what feeds the part of you that picks a direction. Take one step toward something you already love, today, and see that it asked less of you than you thought.
cells.sheetLine: The direction is still there. The walking stopped.
cells.place: in the part of you that says this, not that

cells.tense: You keep moving toward one thing, and you talk about it as if it chose itself.
cells.ask: Say out loud, once, that a choice you've been calling obvious was yours, and leave it at that.
cells.core:
You're already pointed somewhere — in what you keep returning to, what you let drop, where your attention goes when nobody's assigning it. But you describe the direction as if it arrived on its own, something you found rather than something you chose. The pointing is yours. Your name isn't on it.

What's underneath is not a decision you still have to make. It's one you've been making without saying so. The support around you holds a direction better when it's actually named. Say once, out loud, that a choice you've been calling obvious was yours, and let that be enough for this round.
cells.sheetLine: You keep choosing this direction. You call it something you found.
cells.place: in the part of you that says this, not that
